ui_intro: A short film without sound: everything is shown as text in the picture. You can pause at any time or choose a chapter.
k1_p1: The service brake of the truck has two separate brake circuits.
k1_p2: In the example, one circuit belongs to the front axle and one to the rear axle.
k1_p3: When the driver presses the pedal, both circuits get pressure.
k1_p4: If one circuit leaks, its air escapes. The other circuit stays filled.
k1_p5: The truck still brakes, but more weakly. The braking distance gets longer.
k1_p6: It does not pull to the side. The driver stops at once.
k2_p1: Two compressed-air lines lead to the trailer.
k2_p2: Red is the supply line. It keeps the air reservoir of the trailer filled.
k2_p3: Yellow is the brake line. Its pressure rises only when braking.
k2_p4: The trailer brakes with the air from its own reservoir. Yellow only says how hard.
k2_p5: When the driver releases the pedal, yellow is vented and the trailer brake releases.
k3_p1: If the pressure in the red line drops, the trailer brakes by itself.
k3_p2: It uses the air from its own air reservoir.
k3_p3: That is why an uncoupled trailer is braked.
k4_merk: Two brake circuits: if one fails, the other brakes. Red fills, yellow brakes. If red drops, the trailer brakes by itself.
